mentions.name: Letters Practice
mentions.description: A spaced-repetition (SRS) web app for early literacy acquisition that teaches the highest-yield phonetic mapping skills and nothing else. Sessions are kept short (recommended daily cap of n minutes for a child aged n), deliberately avoid engagement tricks for kids, and are designed primarily for parent-child co-use while deferring the social and cultural aspects of learning to read to parents.
mentions.audience: Verbal but pre-literate kids, mostly for parent-child co-use, with older kids able to drive their own sessions.
mentions.source_excerpt: I am working on an SRS based early literacy acquisition webapp: https://letterspractice.com

evidence.value: I am working on an SRS based early literacy acquisition webapp: https://letterspractice.com
evidence.author: NiloCK

mentions.name: Letters Practice
mentions.description: An early literacy app built on the Skuilder tutoring framework, near production readiness, designed to teach reading to verbal but non-literate children. It aims to hit >= 75% efficacy of Mentava at <= 1% of the price, and the author is sharing early access with families of pre-literate kids.
mentions.problem: Early literacy tools like Mentava are expensive; this app aims to deliver >= 75% of that efficacy at <= 1% of the price.
mentions.source_excerpt: With this framework, I'm making (among other things) an early literacy app at https://letterspractice.com. My aim here is to hit >= 75% efficacy of Mentava at <= 1% of the price.

evidence.value: With this framework, I'm making (among other things) an early literacy app at https://letterspractice.com. My aim here is to hit >= 75% efficacy of Mentava at <= 1% of the price.

mentions.name: LettersPractice
mentions.description: A minimalist early literacy app designed family-first: it presumes an adult supervisor who co-learns and acts as a phonetic coach both at and away from the app, putting considered rails on the parent-child reading experience.
mentions.audience: Families with young children learning early literacy, with an adult supervisor acting as phonetic coach.
mentions.source_excerpt: The first [2] is LettersPractice - a minimalist early literacy app that's family-first, in so far as it presumes an adult supervisor who co-learns strong confidence as a phonetic coach both at and away from the app. Putting considered rails on the parent-child reading experience.

evidence.value: The first [2] is LettersPractice - a minimalist early literacy app that's family-first, in so far as it presumes an adult supervisor who co-learns strong confidence as a phonetic coach both at and away from the app. Putting considered rails on the parent-child reading experience.
